body.statement:
For every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), every admissible \(B\), and every \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\), one has \(A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\), \(\mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)=\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O\), and hence \(\widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\). Every adjacency and unshielded collider on every full domain \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances, is preserved, and for every \(k\in[K]\),
\[
 Z_k=T_k(\widetilde\eta)\cup
 \bigl((F_k(\widetilde\eta)\setminus T_k(\widetilde\eta))
 \cap A(\widetilde\eta)\bigr).
\]
Consequently, if \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\ne\varnothing\), then a fully specified faithful replacement witness with all these properties exists. No equality between \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)\) and \(\kappa(\eta)\) is asserted.
body.justification: The proved lemma characterizes every member of a replacement realization fiber and makes existence conditional on nonemptiness.
body.gap: It does not establish realization-fiber nonemptiness.
body.consumer: It transfers any separately supplied faithful realization into the fixed-\(A\) compatibility fiber.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). By the definition of the realization fiber,
\[
 \bigl(G_0(\widetilde\eta),(T_k(\widetilde\eta))_{k=1}^{K}\bigr)
 =\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B),
 \qquad
 \widetilde\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}.
\tag{1}
\]
The admissibility of \(B\) is exactly the hypothesis of the graphical replacement lemma. Applying that lemma to (1) gives
\[
 A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)
\tag{2}
\]
and, for every \(j=0,\ldots,K\),
\[
 \operatorname{skel}(M_j(\widetilde\eta))
 =\operatorname{skel}(M_j(\eta)),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{UC}(M_j(\widetilde\eta))
 =\operatorname{UC}(M_j(\eta))
\tag{3}
\]
on the complete domain \(U_j\). In particular, (3) includes all adjacencies and unshielded colliders involving \(\zeta_j\) when \(j\ge1\).

Membership in \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) in (1) supplies positive selection probability, so the observational selected law is defined; it also supplies non-target kernel stability and faithfulness of every pooled selected law. By the definition of the oracle signature, (3) therefore yields
\[
 \mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)
 =\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_j(\widetilde\eta)),
         \operatorname{UC}(M_j(\widetilde\eta))\bigr)_{j=0}^{K}
 =\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2) and (4), together with the definitions of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\), imply
\[
 \widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta).
\tag{5}
\]
Finally, the target-and-descendant conclusion of the graphical replacement lemma gives, for every \(k\in[K]\),
\[
 Z_k=T_k(\widetilde\eta)\cup
 \bigl((F_k(\widetilde\eta)\setminus T_k(\widetilde\eta))
 \cap A(\widetilde\eta)\bigr).
\tag{6}
\]
This proves the asserted property of every member of \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). If that set is nonempty, choosing any member proves the final existence implication. At no point was \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)=\kappa(\eta)\) used. \(\square\)
